In RobustPrune (Algorithm 2), after p\* is added to N_out(p), the procedure checks every remaining candidate p′ in 𝒱. **A candidate p′ is removed from 𝒱 if α · d(p\*, p′) ≤ d(p, p′).** (p. 4)

In other words, p′ is dropped when the new neighbour p\* is closer to p′ than p is, by at least a factor of α.

**Related details:**
- **Degree check first:** Before any removals, the loop breaks if |N_out(p)| = R, so p never gets more than R out-neighbours. (p. 4)
- **What α is:** α ≥ 1 is a distance threshold. Setting α > 1 is meant to make the distance to the query shrink by a multiplicative factor at every node on the search path, which keeps the graph's diameter small. (p. 4)
- **Comparison with the SNG rule:** The sparse neighbourhood graph rule removes p′ when d(p, p′) > d(p\*, p′). (p. 3) HNSW and NSG implicitly use α = 1. (p. 5)
